notes:
- Your agent can tell you about mail it is not going to answer. Email Manager has a new setting for
  what reaches you: only mail that needs a reply, which is what it did before and is still what a
  new install does; anything a real person wrote; or everything your ignore list did not drop.
  Until now, mail your agent decided needed no reply was dropped without a word, so a decision that
  went wrong looked exactly like an agent that had stopped working.
- Email Replies is now called Email Manager. Answering is one of the three things it does, beside
  watching what arrives and filing it away, alongside answering.
- Its settings are in six named groups instead of one long column, and every on-off setting is a
  switch at the end of its row instead of a tick box.
- An email your agent is not handing you a draft for now gets two or three sentences instead of one
  line, and they carry the date, amount or deadline that was in the message.
- Your ignore list and the limit on how many messages an hour your agent sends you are visible even
  when automatic drafts are off. Both were being applied the whole time, from boxes you could not
  see.
- Times your agent writes for somebody else say which zone they are in. A reply offering "9am" left
  the person reading it to work out whether that meant your morning or theirs.
- Installing an add-on no longer asks you something you have already told this agent. An answer you
  gave once is filled in for the next add-on that asks the same question.
- You can stop one agent reading the web. On that agent's page, under Response quality, "Don't let
  this agent read the web" turns off opening pages and searching, for that agent and for every
  skill you install later. Email, calendar and chat keep working, and so do the services you
  connected yourself on the Connections tab. Worth turning on if the computer running Archie
  belongs to your work.
- Fixed: every question you asked about an Outlook mailbox failed before it left Archie. Asking
  whether a message had arrived from somebody sent Outlook a request in a shape it rejects, and
  your agent then reported the mailbox as unreadable and named the address, which invited you to
  reconnect an account that was never broken. Watching an Outlook inbox was never affected, which
  is how both could be true on the same account at the same time.
- Fixed: the list of who can message your agent could show a stranger's phone number under your own
  name. A Telegram account id is ten digits, the same shape as a phone number here, so it was drawn
  as one. The number was real, and it belonged to somebody who has never heard of Archie.
- Fixed: your agent could be watching no inboxes at all while the panel said it was on. If you had
  chosen which inboxes to watch and later reconnected those accounts, the saved choice pointed at
  accounts that no longer existed. It watches all of them now, and says so.
- The Activity log, on the agent's Setup tab, now says what your email watching is actually doing:
  which inboxes it is watching, when it is taking its first look at a mailbox and holding back
  everything already sitting in there, and when it has lost track of one. The first look is what
  catches people out. Send yourself a test message before it happens and that message is already
  behind, so nothing arrives and nothing is wrong.
- Fixed: pressing Draft on an email your agent had decided needed no reply did nothing at all. It
  asked itself the same question again and got the same answer. Pressing Draft is your decision, so
  it writes the draft now.
- Fixed: Text Replies could go quiet with nothing wrong. A sign-in that had expired, or a dropped
  connection, looked exactly like a text that needed no answer.
- Fixed: a summary sent to Telegram could arrive with stray underscores through it, once summaries
  became long enough to run to a second line.
- Fixed: replacing the token for a chat app your agent is already on emptied the list of who is
  allowed to message it, and the screen said the opposite. It now names who would have to claim the
  agent again, before you press save, and sends you to the claim code afterward.
- Fixed: a question about what was said on a past call could be handed to your calendar instead of
  to the add-on that reads call transcripts.
- Fixed: the video skills could not run on any computer that downloaded their tools rather than
  building them, which is every computer but a developer's. Video Synthesizer works again.
